source.title: Geometric Bogomolov conjecture in arbitrary characteristics
source.version: arXiv v1 submitted 22 August 2021; 29-page preprint, title page dated 24 August 2021
source.publishedConcordance: Publisher title/authors/DOI and journal placement checked. The final 31-page journal text was not available for a line-by-line comparison; no assertion that the suspect v1 proof passages survive in the journal version.
source.byteProvenance: Read through arXiv PDF parsed text and HTML; PDF page 26 was visually checked. Direct download to local scratch failed (network/DNS); no original-PDF SHA-256 is claimed. Obtain and hash the exact final author/publication source before completing this checkpoint.

summary: Full first-pass extraction of the 29-page arXiv v1 and source-routing checkpoint. All numbered results of §§1–5 are represented, with multipart conclusions split and the key height/intersection/descent inputs exposed. The public v1’s field-of-specialness argument needs correction; the journal edition and several original prerequisite proof interiors remain unverified. No library implementation, closed blueprint or design-readiness is claimed.

nearMisses.checked: Definition and hypotheses read at the pinned commit after a current-branch search.
nearMisses.whyNotEnough: It is a point-height construction for an affine Weierstrass curve under AdmissibleAbsValues, normalized to (O). It does not construct canonical heights of arbitrary-dimensional subvarieties or Chow trace; the (O) versus 2(O) convention must be respected.

items.name: Abelian variety over a field
items.statement: For a field F, an abelian variety is a proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec F. Its smoothness, geometric connectedness and commutativity are consequences, not extra replacement carriers.
items.note: Statements read at f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369, TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AbelianVariety/Basic.lean. This does not provide abelian schemes, trace, projectivity or a polarization.

items.name: Isogeny of abelian varieties
items.statement: A homomorphism of abelian varieties over a field is an isogeny when its scheme morphism is finite and surjective.
items.note: Read at the Tau Ceti pin. Symmetry of the isogenous relation and descent of an isogeny are separate obligations.

items.name: Invertible sheaf on a scheme
items.statement: A line bundle on a scheme Z is an invertible O_Z-module, using the full category of invertible sheaves.
items.note: Read at the Tau Ceti pin. The carrier alone gives neither positivity nor numerical equivalence.

items.name: Polarized function field
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed and K/k finitely generated of positive transcendence degree b. A polarization is a normal projective integral k-variety S with an identification k(S)=K and an ample line bundle M on S.

items.name: Projective model of an abelian variety and bundle
items.statement: For A/K and L on A, choose a projective integral k-variety 𝒜 with a projective map π:𝒜→S and an identification of its generic fibre with A, together with a line bundle ℒ restricting to L. For integral X⊂A use its scheme-theoretic closure 𝒳 in 𝒜.

items.name: Normalized geometric subvariety height
items.statement: For integral X⊂A of dimension d and deg_L(X)>0, set h_(ℒ,M)(X)=(c1(ℒ)^(d+1)c1(π*M)^(b−1)[𝒳])/((d+1)deg_L(X)). All intersections are degrees on the k-model. For geometric subvarieties retain the finite field-of-definition and extension-degree normalization.

items.name: Canonical height of a subvariety
items.statement: For symmetric ample L, define hhat_L^M(X)=lim_(n→∞) h_(ℒ,M)([n]X)/n², where [n]X is the image subvariety. For a geometric X the source uses its smallest K-defined enclosing subvariety; prove agreement with finite-extension normalization.

items.name: Existence of the canonical subvariety height
items.statement: Under the polarized function-field hypotheses and for symmetric ample L, the displayed limit exists, is independent of the projective model and extending bundle, and is nonnegative.
items.locator: XY §1.1, p.2, citing Gubler 2003 Theorem 11.18 / Gubler 2007 Theorem 3.6
items.note: These are separate theorem exports in the blueprint. The originals are listed in the unread-proof ledger; no assertion that a citation alone closes the proof.

items.name: Canonical height under finite extension
items.statement: For finite K′/K, pull back the polarization along the normalization of S in K′. Intersection degrees on the new base are divided by [K′:K] to recover the absolute height of a geometric subvariety. Prove invariance under a further extension and include inseparable extensions.
items.locator: XY §1.1 and §§4.3,5, repeated finite extensions; Conrad §9 normalization
items.note: Do not confuse the unnormalized height attached to a new polarized base with the normalized geometric height. Vanishing is unaffected by a positive extension-degree factor.

items.name: Pullback, product and torsion-translation formulas
items.statement: Canonical point heights satisfy hhat_(u*L)(x)=hhat_L(u(x)) for a homomorphism u, addition under tensor products, and hhat_(p1*L1⊗p2*L2)(x,y)=hhat_L1(x)+hhat_L2(y). For symmetric ample L, translation by a torsion point preserves the height.
items.locator: XY §5.1, proof of Lemma 5.3 and reduction to (e)
items.note: The number-field versions in GZ.1 are inputs to a comparison, not a proof over algebraically closed constants.

items.name: Small-point locus
items.statement: For ε>0, X(ε) consists of x∈X(Kbar) such that hhat_L^M(x)<ε. Dense small points means X(ε) is Zariski dense in X for every positive ε.
items.note: The inequality is strict; the zero-height locus is not the definition.

items.name: Independence of dense small points from height choices
items.statement: For fixed A/K/k, changing symmetric ample L or ample polarization M changes nonnegative point heights by positive multiplicative bounds sufficient to make dense-small-points independent of these choices.
items.note: An additive O(1) comparison does not preserve arbitrarily small thresholds. Specify and prove positive multiplicative comparison.

items.name: Chow Kbar/k-trace
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over Kbar and algebraically closed k⊂Kbar, construct an abelian variety Tr over k and a homomorphism tr:Tr_Kbar→A universal for homomorphisms B_Kbar→A with B/k abelian. Factorization is unique.
items.note: The universal property is for homomorphisms, not all morphisms with arbitrary translation. Trace/image are not field traces or linear-algebra traces.

items.name: Trace map in characteristic zero and p
items.statement: For the algebraically closed constant-field setup, tr is a closed immersion in characteristic zero; in characteristic p it is a purely inseparable isogeny onto its image. Do not turn the latter into an embedding.

items.name: Trace under isogenies, subvarieties and quotients
items.statement: An isogeny induces an isogeny of traces; if A has trivial geometric constant trace, an abelian subvariety and an abelian quotient of A have trivial trace. The trace image is a constant-up-to-isogeny abelian subvariety.
items.locator: XY §3.2 and §5.1 last paragraph; Yamaki 2016b Remark 5.4
items.note: Use Poincaré reducibility and functoriality, keeping purely inseparable kernels visible.

items.name: Torsion subvariety
items.statement: A torsion subvariety of A_Kbar is τ+B, with τ a torsion Kbar-point and B an abelian subvariety. The zero-dimensional and whole-variety cases are included.

items.name: Special subvariety over constants
items.statement: X⊂A_Kbar is special over k when X=tr(Y_Kbar)+T for an integral closed subvariety Y of the k-trace and a torsion subvariety T. The trace and the constant field are part of the predicate.

items.name: Special subvarieties have dense small points
items.statement: Under the function-field hypotheses, every special subvariety has dense small points for any symmetric ample L and ample polarization M.
items.locator: XY §1.1, p.3, citing Lang, Fundamentals, Ch.VI Theorem 5.4
items.note: Use constant-point height zero, torsion translations and density; do not assume a number-field small-points result.

items.name: Geometric Bogomolov theorem in arbitrary characteristic
items.statement: For k algebraically closed, K/k finitely generated of positive transcendence degree, A/K abelian and integral closed X⊂A_Kbar, dense small points imply that X is special. Together with special-small this gives the equivalence.
items.locator: XY Theorem 1.1, p.3; proof completed §5.3, p.27

items.name: Chow groups and intersection operations
items.statement: For varieties over a field form cycles modulo rational equivalence; use CH_i(−)_Q, proper pushforward, flat pullback and the intersection product on a smooth variety, with projection and base-change formulas.
items.note: Only the exact existing plan is imported. The reviewed audit distinguishes raw cycle carriers from the absent general Chow/intersection API.

items.name: Effective preorder on rational Chow classes
items.statement: Write α≥0 in CH_i(B)_Q if α is represented by an effective rational i-cycle, and α≤β if β−α≥0. Do not replace this with numerical pseudo-effectivity.

items.name: Fibre-dimension jumping loci
items.statement: For a projective surjective f:X→Y of integral varieties and e=dimX−dimY, put Y_l={y:dim f^−1(y)≥l}. These are closed, Y_e=Y, and for l≥e+1 every nonempty Y_l satisfies dimY_l+l≤dimX−1.

items.name: Proper part of an intersection cycle
items.statement: For integral X in smooth B and effective Cartier divisors H1,…,Hr, sum only components of X∩H1∩…∩Hr of expected dimension dimX−r, with their intersection multiplicities, to obtain (H1…Hr·X)^prop.
items.note: Separate Serre intersection multiplicity from the length of a scheme-theoretic fibre; report §4 records the verification boundary.

items.name: Dimensions of dominating fibre components
items.statement: Let g:B→Y be flat between smooth projective k-varieties, k algebraically closed, X⊂B integral, f=g|X surjective, e=dimX−dimY. Let integral V⊂Y not lie in Y_(e+1). Every component Zi of f^−1(V) dominating V has dimZi=dimV+e.

items.name: Non-proper fibre intersection inequality
items.statement: In p21-dimension assume V∩Y_(e+1) is finite and contained in the smooth locus of V. Then Σ mi[Zi]≤g*[V]·[X] in CH_(dimV+e)(B)_Q, where the source calls mi the multiplicity of Zi in f^−1(V).
items.note: Retain the finite smooth-intersection hypothesis. The coefficient convention is a blocking source-reconciliation issue: the length interpretation is false for a finite nonflat surface cover with generic degree 4 and special fibre length 6 (report §5). A corrected Serre-positive-weight version may suffice for §5 of XY, but is not silently substituted for the source statement.

items.name: General complete intersection through a subvariety
items.statement: Let Y be projective, V⊂Y integral of codimension r≥1, Y smooth at ηV, and Z1,…,Zm integral such that (union Zi)∩V is finite and lies in Ysm∩Vsm. If H is Cartier and O_Y(H)⊗I_V globally generated, r general sections cut divisors H1,…,Hr meeting properly.

items.name: Effective residual cycle meeting prescribed loci properly
items.statement: With the hypotheses of p22-complete, the complete intersection cycle is [V]+W with W effective, V not a component of W, and W meeting every Zi properly.

items.name: Local equations and general-section avoidance
items.statement: At a smooth point of V lying in Ysm, r suitable sections of I_V(H) generate I_V locally by Nakayama; choose such sections simultaneously at the finite prescribed set and ηV. General hyperplane avoidance then excludes unwanted positive-dimensional residual intersections.
items.note: The local and avoidance statements become separate nodes when blueprinted; infinitude of the algebraically closed base is used.

items.name: Globally generated divisors preserve effectivity
items.statement: For smooth projective B and Cartier H with globally generated O_B(H), H·α is effective for every effective rational Chow class α.

items.name: Proper-part inequality
items.statement: For smooth projective B, integral X⊂B and globally generated effective Cartier H1,…,Hr, (H1…Hr·X)^prop≤H1…Hr·[X] in CH_(dimX−r)(B)_Q.

items.name: Expected dimension over a transverse subvariety
items.statement: For the surjective f:X→Y above, if W⊂Y meets every Y_l with l≥e+1 properly, then dim f^−1(W)=dimW+e.

items.name: Top fibre components dominate
items.statement: Under p25-dimension, every irreducible component of f^−1(W) of dimension dimW+e dominates W.

items.name: Residual intersection versus fibre cycle
items.statement: In the proof of Proposition 2.1, identify g*[W]·[X] with the correctly weighted cycle of the residual inverse image, and identify the dominating part over V. Account for the higher-Tor assertion at the generic points before equating a fibre length with an intersection multiplicity.
items.locator: XY proof of Proposition 2.1, p.11; Fulton 1984 Proposition 7.1(b)
items.note: Do not infer Tor vanishing from expected dimension alone. The report computes R=k+(x,y)^2 as an A=k[x²,y²]-module: A⊕Axy⊕(a,b)x⊕(a,b)y. Its special fibre has length 6 but Tor Euler characteristic 4. The source’s intended intersection-coefficient convention must be fixed.

items.name: Descent up to isogeny
items.statement: For k⊂K, A/K is defined over k up to isogeny when there exists A0/k abelian with A isogenous over K to (A0)_K. Record the comparison homomorphism and its field of definition.

items.name: Common isogeny descent field
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, K/k of finite transcendence degree, and algebraically closed intermediate fields k1,k2 with k1∩k2=k. If Ai/ki are abelian and (A1)_K∼(A2)_K, there is A0/k with Ai∼(A0)_ki for i=1,2.
items.note: The source proof passes to a flat quasi-finite model over a product. A finite-type descent construction and its hypotheses must be supplied; do not assert an algebraically closed positive-transcendence field is finitely generated.

items.name: Uniqueness of common descent up to isogeny
items.statement: The A0 in p32-exists is unique up to k-isogeny.

items.name: Isogeny descends over algebraically closed constants
items.statement: If A1,A2/k are abelian over algebraically closed k and become isogenous over any extension K/k, then they are already isogenous over k.

items.name: Spreading and specializing an isogeny
items.statement: Descend a given isogeny between constant abelian varieties to a finitely generated intermediate field; extend it to an isogeny over a nonempty finite-type integral k-scheme after shrinking; specialize at a k-point to get an isogeny of the original varieties.
items.note: All schemes/morphisms and the finite/surjective conditions are spread, not just coordinate functions. A nonempty k-variety has a closed k-point because k is algebraically closed.

items.name: Intersection-field descent of a finite-dimensional subspace
items.statement: Let k1,k2⊂K satisfy k1∩k2=k. If a K-subspace W⊂V0⊗k K for finite-dimensional V0/k is obtained by scalar extension from both ki, then it is obtained from k.
items.note: The elementary proof uses uniqueness of reduced row echelon form rather than needing a new Grassmannian.

items.name: Intersection-field descent without finite dimension
items.statement: The preceding subspace-descent statement holds for arbitrary V0/k, by applying it to intersections with finite-dimensional k-subspaces and their scalar extensions.

items.name: Descent of a fixed closed subvariety to a field intersection
items.statement: Let k1∩k2=k⊂K and Y/k be a variety. If the same closed subvariety X⊂Y_K descends as an embedded subvariety to both ki, it descends to k. On an affine Y=Spec R0, its ideal is generated over K by I∩R0; glue these descended ideals.
items.note: Abstract isomorphism of two models is not enough; the embeddings in a fixed k-model are part of the statement.

items.name: Minimum algebraically closed isogeny field
items.statement: For algebraically closed K/k and A/K abelian there is an algebraically closed intermediate kA of finite transcendence degree over k such that, for every algebraically closed intermediate k′, A descends up to isogeny to k′ iff kA⊂k′.

items.name: Minimum field of a fixed embedded subvariety
items.statement: For algebraically closed K/k, Y/k and X⊂Y_K, there is an algebraically closed intermediate kX of finite transcendence degree over k such that X descends as an embedded subvariety to k′ iff kX⊂k′.

items.name: Relatively algebraically closed intermediate fields
items.statement: I(K/k) consists of intermediate fields k′⊂K containing k such that every element of K algebraic over k′ lies in k′. Do not identify this poset with all algebraically closed subfields of a fixed Kbar without proving the asserted correspondence.

items.name: Stabilizer and quotient of a subvariety
items.statement: Construct the closed subgroup scheme Stab(X)={a:a+X=X}, its connected reduced abelian part in the stated geometric setup, the quotient abelian variety, and the image of X. Distinguish the possibly nonreduced stabilizer from its reduced abelian part in characteristic p.
items.note: The source writes Stab⁰; smooth/reduced conventions must be reconciled before passing to an abelian-variety quotient.

items.name: Specialness under quotient, isogeny and torsion translation
items.statement: Specialness is invariant under isogeny (for an image subvariety), under translation by torsion, and under replacing X by its image modulo its connected reduced stabilizer, with the appropriate quotient ambient abelian variety.

items.name: Minimum torsion envelope
items.statement: For integral X⊂A over an algebraically closed field construct the smallest torsion subvariety containing X. Intersect torsion cosets, choose the component containing X, and use dimension descent; retain finite components and uniqueness.

items.name: Least field of specialness: source target requiring repair
items.statement: For k relatively algebraically closed in K, A/K abelian and X⊂A_Kbar integral, the source asserts existence of k_(A,X)∈I(K/k) such that X is special for A/K/k′ iff k_(A,X)⊂k′ for every k′∈I(K/k).
items.note: This is the exact source theorem target, NOT an endorsement of its printed proof. Its identification k_(A,X)=kA in the nonconstant branch fails for the generic-point example in the report. The asserted initial poset bijection also needs repair; no dependent blueprint may silently import it as verified.

items.name: Geometrically integral generic member of a pencil
items.statement: For normal projective integral S/k of dimension b>1 over algebraically closed k and a very ample M, choose s0 with integral hyperplane section and s1 independent. Blow up their codimension-two base ideal to resolve S⇢P¹; its generic member is geometrically integral and has function field K=k(S), viewed over k(P¹).
items.locator: XY Lemma 3.7 proof, pp.17–18; Jouanolou Theorem 6.10, Hartshorne II.7.17.3
items.note: The base-ideal Cartier property on pencil members, generic integrality and flatness over the smooth curve are separate obligations. Check normality or pass through normalization when calling the generic member a polarization.

items.name: Infinitely many one-dimensional constant subfields
items.statement: The pencil construction yields infinitely many distinct relatively algebraically closed k′⊂K with trdeg(k′/k)=1. Include an argument that varying pencils changes the embedded subfield, not just the parameter coordinate on one P¹.

items.name: Pencil divisor class
items.statement: The associated geometrically integral H⊂S_(k′) is a codimension-one divisor linearly equivalent to M_(k′).

items.name: Pencil generic field identification
items.statement: The composite H→S_(k′)→S identifies generic fields k′(H)=K and exhibits k′ as relatively algebraically closed in K.

items.name: Height decreases on changing constants by a pencil
items.statement: For any A/K, symmetric ample L and integral geometric X⊂A, hhat_L^(S,M)(X)≥hhat_L^(H,M|H)(X), with the precise normal-model and finite-extension normalization.
items.locator: XY Lemma 3.7 final assertion and proof, pp.17–19

items.name: Horizontal closure is dominated by the total section cycle
items.statement: After the pencil base change, the closure 𝒳_H* of the generic X is a component of the proper hyperplane section of 𝒳_(k′); the difference of fundamental cycles is effective. Intersecting with the indicated ample bundles yields the naive-height inequality, hence the canonical inequality.
items.locator: XY last part of Lemma 3.7 proof, pp.18–19
items.note: Track the generic multiplicity and positive degrees; the geometric fibre being integral is not a blanket claim that every base change of 𝒳 is integral.

items.name: Reduction of transcendence degree using two constant fields
items.statement: For algebraically closed k, finitely generated K/k with trdeg≥2 and A/K, choose relatively algebraically closed k1,k2⊂K of transcendence degree one, independent of X, such that validity of geometric Bogomolov for X over both K kbar_i/kbar_i implies validity over K/k.
items.note: The printed last contradiction line needs “not special”. A possible direct two-field proof avoiding the defective general Proposition 3.6 proof is described, with its remaining descent lemmas, in the report.

items.name: Abelian scheme
items.statement: Use a smooth proper group scheme with geometrically connected fibres over the base; in §4 the base S is a smooth projective integral curve over k, with generic point η. Projectivity/relative ampleness is stated when used.

items.name: Multiplication and torsion of abelian schemes
items.statement: For m∈Z construct [m] and 𝒜[m]. For m≠0 multiplication is finite locally free of rank m^(2g), and is étale when m is invertible on the base.

items.name: Integral finite flat multisection
items.statement: A multisection T of π:𝒜→S is a closed integral subscheme with T→S finite flat. Its degree is the positive rank of this finite flat map, not the number of visible geometric points.

items.name: Torsion multisection and order
items.statement: The multisection inclusion determines a T-point of 𝒜_T. It is torsion if [m] kills that point for some integer m≥1; its order is the least positive such m.

items.name: Closure and étaleness of torsion multisections
items.statement: A torsion multisection is the closure of its generic torsion closed point. If its order is prime to char k, it is contained in the finite étale group scheme 𝒜[m], hence is finite étale over normal S and smooth over k.
items.note: For p-primary torsion do not claim this étaleness conclusion; use a finite extension making the torsion point a section instead.

items.name: Symmetric and antisymmetric line bundles
items.statement: For inversion ι=[−1] on an abelian scheme, ℒ is symmetric if ι*ℒ≅ℒ and antisymmetric if ι*ℒ≅ℒ^∨. This concerns bundle isomorphisms, not a choice of positive metric.

items.name: Zero-section rigidification
items.statement: For the zero section e:S→𝒜, a rigidification of ℒ is an isomorphism e*ℒ≅O_S. Morphisms and base change preserve this chosen trivialization.
items.note: A naked Prop field is not the data of a rigidification; recover A2’s Poincaré conventions rather than a second spelling.

items.name: Relative square/cube and seesaw interfaces
items.statement: For the projective abelian schemes used here import the square/cube identities. A bundle fibrewise trivial is pulled back from the base under the seesaw hypotheses; if rigidified, that base bundle is trivial.
items.locator: XY Lemma 4.1 proof, p.20; Lang Abelian Varieties §7
items.note: The actual cohomology/base-change hypotheses in seesaw must be verified; not every proper family has this property.

items.name: Multiplication formula for rigidified symmetric bundles
items.statement: For any integer m and rigidified symmetric ℒ on 𝒜/S, [m]*ℒ≅ℒ^(m²).

items.name: Multiplication formula for rigidified antisymmetric bundles
items.statement: For any integer m and rigidified antisymmetric ℒ, [m]*ℒ≅ℒ^m, including m=0 and negative m.

items.name: Integral symmetric/antisymmetric decomposition
items.statement: For any rigidified ℒ, the bundles ℒ⊗ι*ℒ and ℒ⊗(ι*ℒ)^∨ are respectively symmetric and antisymmetric and their tensor product is ℒ². Do not divide by two in the integral Picard group.

items.name: Restriction to a torsion multisection
items.statement: The restriction of any rigidified ℒ to a torsion multisection is torsion in Pic(T). For a multisection of order m, the square of the restricted bundle is killed by m², so a safe integral annihilator is 2m².
items.note: The annihilator is a derived test from the source’s symmetric/antisymmetric proof, not a claimed optimal exponent.

items.name: Relative ampleness plus rigidification gives nefness
items.statement: On an abelian scheme over a smooth projective curve, a symmetric rigidified relatively ample bundle is nef on the total scheme.
items.note: It need not be ample on the total space: its restriction to the zero section has degree zero.

items.name: Nef domination of a symmetric rigidified bundle
items.statement: For symmetric rigidified relatively ample ℒ and any symmetric rigidified ℒ′, there is an integer a>0 with aℒ−ℒ′ nef.

items.name: Pullback and limiting argument for nefness
items.statement: Choose N ample on S with ℒ⊗π*N ample. Pulling back along [m] and using the symmetric identity shows ℒ+(1/m²)π*N nef; the nef cone is closed, so ℒ is nef.
items.note: Rational numerical divisor classes are used only at this limiting step; ℒ itself remains an actual invertible sheaf.

items.name: Numerical class of a torsion multisection
items.statement: For π:𝒜→S of relative dimension g≥1, symmetric rigidified ℒ and torsion multisection T, c1(ℒ)^g≡(deg(ℒ_η)/deg(T/S))[T] as numerical classes of one-cycles. Here deg(ℒ_η) is its top self-intersection; relative ampleness is not required for this equality.
items.note: Numerical equivalence, not equality in CH_1(𝒜)_Q. The coefficient can vanish without ampleness. The paragraph about Grushevsky–Zakharov is a stronger contextual result, not silently imported.

items.name: Vanishing against rigidified test bundles
items.statement: For symmetric rigidified ℒ and any rigidified test bundle M, c1(ℒ)^g·c1(M)=0 on the (g+1)-dimensional total scheme. For symmetric/antisymmetric M, projection under [m] compares exponents 2g+2 or 2g+1 with degree 2g; the integral square decomposition gives the general case.
items.note: It is the test bundle M that is split; the printed passage switches bundle letters. Take |m|>1 to conclude vanishing.

items.name: Intersections against a base bundle
items.statement: For a bundle N on S, c1(ℒ)^g·π*N=deg(ℒ_η)degN and [T]·π*N=deg(T/S)degN. Every test M is (M−π*e*M)+π*e*M with rigidified first summand, proving p42 by testing all line bundles.

items.name: Abelian model of everywhere good reduction
items.statement: If K=k(S) for a smooth projective curve and A/K has good reduction at every closed point, glue the local abelian models to the unique abelian scheme over S with this generic fibre.
items.note: An abelian model is proper; a general Néron model need not be. Finite ramified base change of an abelian scheme is permitted, unlike an arbitrary Néron-model base-change claim.

items.name: Extending and rigidifying a generic symmetric bundle
items.statement: On the everywhere-good abelian model over the smooth curve, extend a divisor representing the generic symmetric L by closure; regularity makes it Cartier. Subtract π*e*ℒ to rigidify. Use the vertical-bundle/base-pullback assertion to prove symmetry of the rigidified extension.
items.note: Do not deduce symmetry of an arbitrary extension merely from generic symmetry.

items.name: Canonical height equals the rigidified model intersection
items.statement: For symmetric ample L and its symmetric rigidified extension to an everywhere-good abelian model, the normalized model height equals the canonical height because [m]*ℒ≅ℒ^(m²). Include the finite-extension normalization for geometric subvarieties.

items.name: Semistable reduction after finite extension
items.statement: For A over the function field of a smooth projective curve, after a finite extension and normalization of the base, A has semistable reduction at every place. Preserve the separability/valuation hypotheses of the actual source theorem.

items.name: Nowhere-degenerate abelian variety and maximal part
items.statement: Over the algebraic closure of a polarized function field, A is nowhere degenerate when it has potentially good reduction at every divisorial place. Construct its maximal nowhere-degenerate abelian subvariety m. After descending to a one-variable field with semistable reduction everywhere, realize the needed part with everywhere good reduction.
items.locator: XY §5 reduction (d); Yamaki 2016b §1.3 and references to Yamaki 2016a §7
items.note: Do not identify this with good reduction of a chosen model before finite extension. TB.6 supplies local measures, not this maximal subvariety.

items.name: Yamaki reduction to nowhere-degenerate trivial-trace quotient
items.statement: For A over the algebraic closure of a function field, m its maximal nowhere-degenerate abelian subvariety and t the image of the constant trace, t⊂m and geometric Bogomolov for A, for m, and for m/t are equivalent. The quotient m/t is nowhere degenerate and has trivial trace.
items.locator: XY §5, p.23; Yamaki 2016b Theorem 1.5 (=5.5) and Remark 5.4
items.note: Theorem and proof dependency on Yamaki 2016a Theorem E and 2016b Theorem 5.3 were read. Their complete proof interiors remain a prerequisite-paper task, not supplied by the short atlas metric stages.

items.name: Constant/nonconstant product splitting input
items.statement: Let B=B0_Kbar be constant and A nowhere degenerate with trivial trace. Assuming geometric Bogomolov for A, a closed integral X⊂B×A with dense small points equals prB(X)×prA(X), with the first projection constant and the second a torsion coset.
items.locator: Yamaki 2016b Theorem 5.3, used in 5.5; XY §5 reduction (d)
items.note: The relative-height and generic-fibre arguments of Yamaki §§3–5 are not yet fully extracted in this checkpoint.

items.name: Manin–Mumford with trivial geometric trace
items.statement: For k algebraically closed, K/k finitely generated, A/K with trivial Kbar/k-trace and integral X⊂A_Kbar, Zariski density of X(Kbar)∩A(Kbar)_tors implies X is a torsion coset. Validity in characteristic p is essential.
items.note: RP.5 plans selected Manin–Mumford routes but does not pin this all-characteristic trivial-trace input. Add this exact source contract there; a number-field version or Faltings finiteness is insufficient.

items.name: Essential minimum over a curve function field
items.statement: For an integral projective X/Kbar with nonnegative canonical point height, μess(X)=sup_(nonempty open U⊂X) inf_(x∈U(Kbar)) hhat(x). Then dense small points is equivalent to μess=0.

items.name: Fundamental height inequality
items.statement: For K the function field of a smooth projective curve and an ample line bundle with admissible semipositive metric, H(X)/((d+1)deg_L X)≤μess(X), where H is the unnormalized intersection height.
items.note: Restrict the imported proof to transcendence degree one. No higher-base successive-minima theorem is being silently used.

items.name: Converse successive-minima inequality
items.statement: In the same one-variable semipositive setup, let ei be the successive minima defined by removal of codimension-i closed subsets. Then Σ_(i=1)^(d+1) ei≤H(X)/deg_L X. For canonical heights ei≥0, so H(X)=0 implies μess=0.
items.locator: Gubler 2007 Proposition 4.3 and Corollary 4.4, pp.9–10; implicit input to XY §5.3
items.note: This converse is not the inequality stated in XY Lemma 5.2. It is an additional necessary input for applying induction to the zero-height fibres.

items.name: Dense small points imply canonical subvariety height zero
items.statement: For trdeg(K/k)=1, A/K, symmetric ample L and integral geometric X, dense small points imply hhat_L(X)=0.

items.name: Canonical height zero implies dense small points
items.statement: Under the same one-variable canonical-height hypotheses, hhat_L(X)=0 implies dense small points.
items.locator: Gubler 2007 Corollary 4.4; Yamaki 2016b Proposition 2.3; required in XY §5.3

items.name: Height-zero points modulo the constant trace
items.statement: For a finitely generated regular extension K/k of positive transcendence degree with the chosen projective polarization, the canonical quadratic form is positive definite after quotienting A(K) by the image of Tr_(K/k)(A)(k) and tensoring with R. In particular, with trivial geometric trace a geometric point has height zero iff it is torsion, by passing to a finite field of definition.
items.locator: Conrad 2006 Theorem 9.15; XY proofs of Lemma 5.3 and §5.3
items.note: Read Theorem 9.15 and the reductions §§9–10. Do not assert ordinary Northcott finiteness over an arbitrary infinite constant field.

items.name: Iterated sum images
items.statement: For integral X⊂A define X_m as the image of X^m under summation for m≥1 and X_0={0}. Then dimX_(m−1)≤dimX_m≤dimX_(m−1)+dimX.

items.name: Translated sum images stabilize to an abelian subvariety
items.statement: After a finite extension choose x0∈X(K). The irreducible closed subvarieties X_m−mx0 form an increasing sequence stabilizing to B; closure under addition and the dimension argument for the fibre over zero yield closure under inversion, so B is an abelian subvariety.
items.note: The reduced/geometrically integral subgroup structure in characteristic p is part of this construction, not inferred from an arbitrary nonreduced stabilizer.

items.name: Poincaré complete reducibility
items.statement: For B⊂A an abelian subvariety, construct an isogeny A→B×(A/B), equivalently a homomorphism A→B whose restriction to B is an isogeny, with the field-of-definition hypotheses recorded.

items.name: Small points pass to sum images
items.statement: For a nonnegative quadratic canonical point height, hhat(x1+…+xm)≤m Σ hhat(xi). Thus dense small points on X give dense small points on X_m and on X_(m−1)×X, after using the appropriate product heights and functorial comparisons.

items.name: First full sum image is torsion: positive-dimensional branch
items.statement: Under XY reductions (a)–(d), assume dimX>0 and dense small points. There is a unique r≥1 with dimX_(r−1)<dimX_r and X_r a torsion subvariety.
items.locator: XY Lemma 5.3, p.24, with the positive-dimensional branch made explicit
items.note: The lemma is printed without dimX>0, but X={0} has no strict dimension increase. The zero-dimensional case is handled separately in §5.3. The complete printed statement must be reconciled with the final edition.

items.name: Torsion translation making the sum image abelian
items.statement: If X_r=B+τ for torsion τ, choose a torsion σ with [r]σ=τ and replace X by X−σ, after a finite extension if needed. Then X_r=B without changing dense small points or the desired torsion-coset conclusion.

items.name: Two-factor addition map with smaller fibres
items.statement: Put A′=X_r and Y=X_(r−1)×X. The addition map f:Y→A′ is surjective, has generic fibre dimension e=dimX_(r−1)+dimX−dimA′, and e<dimX.
items.note: Y uses the sum-image X_(r−1), not the Cartesian power X^(r−1). The latter does not provide the same dimension bound.

items.name: Codimension of the bad fibre locus
items.statement: For f:Y→A′ above, A′_(e+1) is closed of codimension at least two. For t outside it every irreducible component of f^−1(t) has dimension e.
items.note: Use the general fibre-dimension bound together with the lower bound over a smooth target; do not infer equidimensional fibres solely from dominance.

items.name: Smooth ambient summation morphism
items.statement: Let B=(+:A×A→A)^−1(A′). The map (x,a′)↦(x,a′−x) identifies B with A×A′, so h:B→A′ is smooth and flat and Y embeds in B with f=h|Y.
items.note: The explicit product identification supplies flatness without assuming the subvariety Y is smooth.

items.name: Integral abelian ambient diagram
items.statement: For everywhere-good A over S, the needed abelian subvarieties A′ and B extend to abelian schemes; identify their embeddings with the schematic closures and extend the summation diagram. Let 𝒴 be the closure of Y inside 𝒝.
items.note: Prove the closed-subvariety/good-reduction extension using the abelian/Néron model APIs; closure of an arbitrary generic subscheme is not automatically an abelian scheme.

items.name: Zero-height fibres over prime-to-p torsion
items.statement: Under reductions (a)–(e), for a torsion t∈A′(Kbar) of order prime to char k outside A′_(e+1), every component of f^−1(t) has height zero in A×A.

items.name: Reduction of an arbitrary torsion point to a smooth section
items.statement: For arbitrary torsion t choose finite K′/K over which t is rational; normalize S in K′. Since k is algebraically closed, the resulting normal projective curve is smooth. Pull back the abelian schemes. Properness extends t to a section, killed by its order by separatedness. This section is a smooth closed curve even when the order is divisible by char k. Apply the same intersection proof over S′ and descend height vanishing using normalized finite-extension compatibility.
items.locator: Supplement to XY Proposition 5.4 proof, using §§4.1–4.3 and its finite-extension reductions
items.note: An authored repair proposal, not a quotation from the preprint. It removes the proof’s prime-to-p restriction without asserting p-primary torsion multisections are étale. All normalization and model-closure compatibilities are required.

items.name: Zero-height fibres over all torsion: source target
items.statement: Under reductions (a)–(e), every component of f^−1(t) has height zero for every torsion t outside A′_(e+1), with no prime-to-p qualification.
items.note: The statement is stronger than the explicitly written multisection proof. The preceding finite-base-change construction is the proposed bridge; prime-to-p torsion alone also suffices for the main induction.

items.name: Nef mixed-intersection domination
items.statement: On projective integral Z of dimension q+s, if L and M are nef and bL−M nef, b>0, then 0≤M^q L^s[Z]≤b^q L^(q+s)[Z]. Prove by telescoping the difference into products of nef classes.
items.note: Use q=dimA′ and s=e+1; positive weighted component intersections then vanish individually when the upper bound is zero.

items.name: Positive component multiplicities force individual zero heights
items.statement: In the integral ambient diagram, Proposition 2.1 gives Σ mi[𝒵i]≤h*[T]·[𝒴]. After numerical substitution [T]≡a LA′^q, a>0, intersect with LB^(e+1), apply nef domination and hhat(Y)=0 to conclude each LB^(e+1)[𝒵i]=0.
items.note: Use exactly one factor a after substitution. The displayed intermediate a h*[T] in v1 is not compatible with the preceding [T]≡a LA′^q.

items.name: Prime-to-p torsion is dense
items.statement: For an abelian variety over an algebraically closed field, the union of its prime-to-characteristic torsion points is Zariski dense; its intersection with a nonempty open remains dense. Torsion cosets contain dense torsion.
items.locator: XY §5.3 torsion-density step; the prime-to-p form suffices for its proof
items.note: This is not a count of rational torsion over the original nonclosed K.

items.name: Density from fibres of a dominant map
items.statement: Let f:Y→Z be a dominant morphism of integral varieties. If D⊂Z is dense and each fibre over D has a dense set of points of a specified subset E⊂Y, then E is dense in Y: for each nonempty open U⊂Y, constructibility and dominance give an open subset of Z inside f(U).

items.name: Dimension induction from torsion fibres
items.statement: Induct on d=dimX. For d=0 use heightzero-point. For d>0, fibres over torsion outside the bad locus have dimension e<d and height zero; use heightzero-small before invoking induction. Dense torsion in these fibres gives dense torsion in Y, then Manin–Mumford makes Y a torsion coset; its second projection is X, so X is a torsion coset.

items.name: Model metrics and canonical measures
items.statement: On the relevant nonarchimedean analytifications construct the line-bundle metrics from formal models, model measures with multiplicity-weighted special-fibre intersections and total mass equal to the generic degree, and semipositive limits with the specified approximation hypotheses.
items.note: This exact local infrastructure is planned; global equidistribution and strict supports are not supplied by it.

items.name: Generic degree and intersection base change
items.statement: Intersection with line bundles commutes with flat base change and proper pushforward in the asserted dimensional range; for a flat family over a curve, fibre top degree is constant.

Embedded-subvariety/linear descent and the generic-image argument refine existing scheme and effective-descent interfaces; no new Grassmannian is required.
The elementary blowup/pencil geometry is a source for the named birational/model stage. The height inequality remains with the function-field height owner.
Isogeny descent, minimum isogeny fields and spreading refine arithmetic Hom and isogeny theory; they do not rebuild the field abelian-variety carrier.

The schematic-closure identification in a good abelian model needs the reduction/model owner, including finite-base-change compatibility.

routes.title: Heights, rational points and obstructions, Part II: function-field heights and trace
routes.brief: Build a function-field extension of Heights, rational points and obstructions, starting from its point-height interfaces rather than repeating them. Fix algebraically closed constants, normal projective polarizations and the extension-degree convention. Construct projective model heights of subvarieties, canonical limits and their independence, mixed canonical intersections, symmetric point heights, product and pullback formulas, Chow K/k-trace with its universal homomorphism and inseparable kernel, and the positive-definite quotient-by-trace theorem of Conrad. For a one-variable function field prove both directions of the height-zero/dense-small-points criterion using Gubler Lemma 4.1, Proposition 4.3 and Corollary 4.4, with normalized versus unnormalized heights stated explicitly. Import the existing abelian-variety carrier, A1–A3/A6, SF.5 intersections, TB.6 model metrics, and GZ.1’s number-field canonical-height design as a comparison rather than treating it as a function-field proof. The pending PAPER-YUAN-26 routes propose related adelic infrastructure but are partial and are not suppliers: before activation, reconcile the shared canonical function-field and mixed-intersection nodes so that one route owns each, ideally by adding these source contracts to that accepted generic owner if it is created. No Yuan-specific uniformity, Faltings-height bigness or twice-theta normalization is assumed here. Every definition gets use-derived API and degenerate, constant-family, finite-extension and non-example tests.
routes.reason: The exact subvariety-height, varying-constants and trace-quotient contracts are absent from RP.0/GZ.1/R35; this reusable extension is shared by geometric and uniform Bogomolov consumers. Activation must reconcile the overlapping partial PAPER-YUAN-26 proposals.

routes.title: Heights, rational points and obstructions, Part II: geometric Bogomolov
routes.brief: Extend the small-points direction of Heights, rational points and obstructions beyond its explicitly number-field RP.5 theorem to Xie–Yuan’s geometric Bogomolov theorem in every characteristic and every positive finite transcendence degree over algebraically closed constants. Import FunctionFieldHeightsAndTrace for heights and traces, A6 for isogeny descent and complete reducibility, RP.5 for torsion cosets/stabilizers and the all-characteristic trivial-trace Manin–Mumford source contract, SF.5 for the non-proper intersection inequality, A1–A3 for the rigidified abelian-scheme bundle theory, and R11.1/R11.3 for good/semistable models. Build specialness and its precise quotient/isogeny invariance, the two-pencil change-of-constants reduction, the nowhere-degenerate maximal subvariety and Yamaki’s reduction to its trace-free quotient, and the two-factor sum-image dimension induction. Give the Yamaki 2016a/2016b proof interior its own stages, importing local analytic metrics and measures from TB.6; do not hide a missing global equidistribution theorem behind that local stage. Keep the statement of Proposition 3.6 as an unresolved source target until the final edition or a corrected proof is checked, and test the generic-point counterexample to the printed k_(A,X)=kA shortcut. A direct two-algebraically-independent-fields proof of the main reduction is a candidate bypass, not a certified replacement yet. State Lemma 5.3 on its positive-dimensional branch and separately discharge dimension zero. Use the Gubler converse before inducting on zero-height fibres; for all torsion orders supply the finite-base-change-to-a-section bridge rather than falsely calling p-primary multisections étale. Numerical cycle equality is never upgraded to rational equivalence. Include an explicit source-concordance phase before blueprint execution.

conventions.varieties: Unless an item gives a different context, XY varieties are integral separated finite-type schemes. Section 2 is over an algebraically closed field; Section 4 is over a smooth projective curve over a field. Geometric subvarieties and their field-of-definition extensions must not be conflated with their K-defined enclosing subschemes.
conventions.sourceVsAuthored: Source targets retain their identifiers even where a proof is questioned. Entries explicitly called a supplement are authored proposed bridges, not claims that the cited preprint proves them.
conventions.multiplicity: A fibre fundamental-cycle coefficient (length) and a Serre intersection coefficient (Euler characteristic of Tor) are distinct. The report gives a six-versus-four diagnostic. Do not execute p21-inequality using lengths until the intended final-source convention is settled.
conventions.height: Write H for the unnormalized intersection height and hhat=H/((dimX+1)deg_L X) for the normalized subvariety height. One-variable successive-minima imports are not asserted over an arbitrary higher-dimensional base.

diagnostics.scope: Public arXiv v1 proof of Proposition 3.6, not a claim about the final journal edition or the main theorem
diagnostics.detail: Over algebraically closed k of characteristic zero let F=acl(k(t)), E/F the nonisotrivial Legendre curve, Ω=acl(F(E)), and P the generic point of E_F regarded as an Ω-point. For A=E_Ω and X={P}, Stab⁰(X)=0 and its minimum torsion envelope is A. A descends to F so kA⊂F, but X is not special over F: every zero-dimensional special subvariety of the constant E_F is an F-rational point, whereas P is generic. This disproves the proof shortcut k_(A,X)=kA in its nonconstant branch.

diagnostics.scope: Invalidity of identifying fibre length with intersection multiplicity; authored diagnostic
diagnostics.detail: Let k have characteristic zero, A=k[a,b]⊂k[x,y] via a=x²,b=y², and R=k+(x,y)². Then R=A⊕Axy⊕(a,b)x⊕(a,b)y has generic rank 4 and R/(a,b)R has basis 1,xy,x³,x²y,xy²,y³, of dimension 6. The Koszul resolutions of the two ideals give Tor₁ dimension 2 and Euler characteristic 4. Homogenize to X=Proj k[z,x²,xy,y²,x³,x²y,xy²,y³] finite over Y=Proj k[z²,x²,y²]≅P²; embed its graph into Y×P^N. The flat smooth ambient projection meets all stated geometric hypotheses of Proposition 2.1, but the length interpretation would require 6≤4 after taking degree. The Serre coefficient is 4 and does not yield that contradiction.
For X={0}, all sum-image dimensions are zero, so the printed strict-increase conclusion has no r. State that lemma with dim X>0 and retain the separate zero-dimensional induction base.
